title: Optimize walkthrough: econ sim + prefix/KV recs - Atlas Retail
summary: Intro demo of Redwood Optimize recommendations applied to Atlas Retail's conversational recommender. Focus on batching and prefix/KV caching economics, walk through simulation numbers for 1k qps and 5k qpm scenarios, discuss tradeoffs between latency SLOs and cost-savings, and next steps for pilot and security review.
topics: Continuous batching parameters (max batch size, batch wait)
Cost model assumptions: tokenization, concurrency, burst vs reserved
Latency SLO implications and fallback policies
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood); Priya, Ethan, Sofia (Atlas)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining we scheduled 50 minutes to walk through the optimize playbook we ran the econ sim for the recommender, hope that's okay?
[00:12] Priya Rao: yep thanks Maya, excited - short background we run a personalized chat + product rec pipeline, latency target 300ms p95 and want to cut token cost without impacting CTR
[00:22] Liam O'Connor: cool, quick agenda: 1) show the console econ sim with your telemetry-ish numbers, 2) propose prefix/KV prefetch settings, 3) run a few what-if cost scenarios and RFCs for pilot
[00:38] Ethan Cole: quick note — we might need private deployment due to data residency for EU customers, but first let's see the hosted numbers
[00:45] Speaker 4: yeah also curious about dedicated reserved pricing
[00:50] Liam O'Connor: perfect, i'll share my screen - pulling up the Optimize console - forgive the noise in the notes, console shows a baseline: 1k qps equivalent, avg prompt tokens 240, avg completion tokens 60, session affinity 1.8 turn per session
[01:10] Priya Rao: those token counts are a touch high for us in long tail but ok as an average
[01:16] Maya Chen: right so first idea is prefix / KV caching for the static context — product taxonomy and user preferences we can cache KV across sessions to avoid re-encoding 120 tokens of context every time
[01:30] Ethan Cole: how much do you normally see saved per call?
[01:33] Liam O'Connor: in our sim, with a 70% cache hit for prefix KV we see about 45% token cost reduction on encoder-side costs and 20-25% end-to-end token cost when factoring completion tokens and batching gains
[01:50] Sofia Martinez: what assumptions for hit rate there? 70% seems optimistic for browsing users
[01:55] Liam O'Connor: fair — sim allows tuning: 40, 55, 70. For Atlas we used 55% as a midline given your sessionization and user churn numbers you shared earlier
[02:06] Priya Rao: can you show the batching curve? we're worried about p95 hitting the 300ms target if we increase batch wait
[02:12] Liam O'Connor: sure — switching to the batching tab. With continuous batching: batch wait 12ms, max batch size 32 we get mean token throughput improvements but p95 stays under 300 for the small model variants. If you need p95 under 150ms then we recommend lower wait 4ms and max batch size 16, which reduces batching benefit but keeps latency tight
[02:40] Maya Chen: to make it concrete i ran a sim for 1k qps steady vs 5k qpm bursty. at 1k qps with 55% KV hit and batch wait 12ms we estimate cost/unit down 32% and p95 260ms. at 5k qpm burst pattern cost per million tokens increases due to more small batches but caching still saves ~18%
[03:05] Ethan Cole: do you include prefix encoding CPU/GPU overhead for caching? like cost to precompute encodings and store them?
[03:11] Liam O'Connor: yes — Optimize factors in prefetch compute cost and storage (small KV entries). There's an amortization across hits; break-even in our sim was about 20 requests per cached key per day
[03:25] Speaker 4: any concerns about cold-starts?
[03:27] Liam O'Connor: cold-starts are modeled: first request pays full encoding, but the system supports proactive prefetch for high-value users or scheduled pre-warm during expected peak windows
[03:40] Priya Rao: what about privacy and keying? we can't persist user identifiers without hashing and consent
[03:46] Maya Chen: good point — for Private deployments you can use customer managed KMS and hashed keys; in Hosted we offer encryption at rest and tokenization policies too, and we can scope KV residency to region
[04:00] Priya Rao: we need SOC2 + ISO27001 docs, and an on-prem option for a subset of traffic
[04:06] Maya Chen: noted — we'll attach the compliance pack (SOC2/ISO, pen test report) post call
[04:12] Sofia Martinez: walk me through a concrete price calc — can you show numbers?
[04:16] Liam O'Connor: yes — showing the cost model. Baseline: 1M requests/day => ~72M tokens/day baseline. Hosted per-token math (synth): $0.6 per 1M input tokens, $0.9 per 1M output tokens for chosen model. With 55% cache hit, effective input tokens drop to 38M, that's about $13 savings/day in that simplified model. Add batching benefit which lowers GPU ops by ~12% in this case so combined saving around $18/day — scales linearly with traffic
[05:00] Ethan Cole: these per-token prices are placeholders right? for committed/dedicated we'd have different unit costs
[05:05] Maya Chen: correct — dedicated reserved gives steeper unit reductions; Optimize can simulate both hosted and dedicated unit economics and show where reserve commitments pay off
[05:14] Priya Rao: i'd like to see a scenario with 85% KV hit for power users and 35% for anonymous users — can you run split-segment sim?
[05:21] Liam O'Connor: yep that's in the segmentation panel — running now... (typing noises) ok results: overall weighted saving becomes 41% on input tokens, cost down 28% after batching; p95 slightly increases for anonymous group but stays sub-350ms.
[05:45] Speaker 4: what about tokenization variance — we have lots of sku descriptions with long tails
[05:48] Liam O'Connor: we added variance envelopes — you can feed a token length distribution CSV and the sim will sample; that shifts the expected savings and shows percentiles for cost outcomes
[06:05] Priya Rao: how do rollouts work? we can't flip KV caching across all customers at once
[06:10] Maya Chen: console supports canary rollouts by segment — you can enable prefix/KV for 10% of sessions, monitor CTR and latency and then expand; automatic rollback if quality regressions exceed threshold
[06:24] Priya Rao: what metrics do you recommend to watch for quality regressions?
[06:27] Liam O'Connor: ask to track: suggestion CTR lift/delta, hallucination rate on a small eval set, latency p95, and token consumption per session. We can instrument trace ids so you can map performance back to prompt sets
[06:44] Sofia Martinez: any competitor caveats we should know?
[06:47] Maya Chen: some providers offer naive caching but don't integrate with batching and routing; others lock you into a single deployment mode. Redwood focuses on unified runtime, plus we have prebuilt prefetched-modes and rollback safety nets
[07:05] Ethan Cole: security: will KV cache entries be visible to Redwood staff?
[07:08] Liam O'Connor: in hosted, cache metadata is encrypted; only aggregated telemetry is visible to our operations team. For strict access you can opt for Private with customer KMS/HSM and restrict access via RBAC
[07:25] Priya Rao: ok let's talk pilot scope timeline
[07:27] Maya Chen: propose a 6-week pilot: week 1 onboarding + data sample upload, week 2 run baseline sim, week 3 deploy prefix KV for 10% canary, weeks 4-5 monitor and iterate, week 6 decision and scale plan
[07:40] Ethan Cole: who needs access to our telemetry? we can't share raw PII logs
[07:44] Liam O'Connor: only tokenized telemetry is needed for the sim — we can accept redacted exports or hashed identifiers. We'll sign an NDA if required
[07:53] Priya Rao: ok good. also curious about autoscaling and burst handling if we use dedicated reserved pools
[07:58] Liam O'Connor: dedicated pools support burst credits and backfill routing to hosted fallback if burst exceeds reserved capacity, with policies you can set to prioritize latency or cost
[08:12] Speaker 4: small tangent — did you account for network egress on on-prem?
[08:15] Maya Chen: on-prem removes egress; VPC-private keeps traffic inside customer's cloud, we only need control plane calls unless you opt-in for metrics export
[08:25] Priya Rao: this is all very helpful. can we get a CSV of the sim runs and the raw assumptions?
[08:29] Maya Chen: yes we'll export and share the simulation CSV, plus the console link and a short runbook for the canary
[08:35] Sofia Martinez: one question — how do you handle model variety? we use two model families depending on query complexity
[08:40] Liam O'Connor: Optimize supports multi-model routing; the sim shows combined economics and per-model breakdowns. Also suggests quantization and smaller model fallbacks for low-complexity queries
[08:52] Priya Rao: what about caching staleness? if product catalog updates hourly do we invalidate keys?
[08:56] Liam O'Connor: TTL policies and event-driven invalidation are supported — you can push catalog change events to invalidate related keys; we recommend short TTL for fast moving items and longer for static user prefs
[09:10] Maya Chen: we have about 30 minutes left, want to dig into the CSV results or go over the pilot SLA?
[09:15] Priya Rao: pilot SLA first, then CSV if time
[09:18] Liam O'Connor: SLA sketch: 99.9% availability for hosted endpoints in pilot, 95th p50/p95 latency targets defined per model, incident reporting, and a rollback TD policy — full enterprise SLA would be part of the dedicated agreement
[09:40] Sofia Martinez: can you clarify data retention on pilot logs? we need 90 day retention for some audit trails
[09:44] Maya Chen: we can configure retention policies per tenant; 90 days is doable for audit logs, longer retention is an add-on
[09:52] Priya Rao: ok final asks from our side: 1) sim CSV with 3 scenarios (low, base, high) + segmented sim for power vs anon, 2) SOC2/ISO pack + on-prem tech brief, 3) pilot SOW and pricing ballpark for 6-week pilot.
[10:10] Maya Chen: great — we'll send those. any blockers to schedule kickoff next week?
[10:14] Ethan Cole: next week works but want to confirm legal touchpoint for data processing agreement
[10:18] Maya Chen: we'll include legal contact in the email and cc our solutions architect.
[10:22] Priya Rao: thanks all — that was productive
[10:24] Maya Chen: thanks for your time, we'll follow up with materials and a proposed kickoff calendar
[10:30] (call ends)
next_steps: Maya to send sim CSV (low/base/high) and console link
Attach compliance pack (SOC2, ISO27001) and on-prem technical brief
Provide pilot SOW and 6-week pricing ballpark
Schedule kickoff and include legal/data processing contact
action_items: Maya Chen: share sim CSV and console link by 2026-03-06
Liam O'Connor: prepare pilot SOW draft by 2026-03-09
Priya Rao: provide token length distribution sample CSV by 2026-03-08
Ethan Cole: confirm internal legal contact and data handling constraints by 2026-03-06
